t: A low-cost Wi-Fi board with a built-in 2.8 inch touch screen.
steps: Buy the board from an online marketplace and check which screen version ships.
Plug it into a USB wall charger or computer with a micro-USB cable.
Try a ready-made project from the community project list with its web flasher.
Install the free Arduino IDE and add the ESP32 board package.
Install the CH340 USB driver on computers that do not see the board.
Choose ESP32 Dev Module as the board type.
Copy the display setup file from the community guide and run the hello world example.
Calibrate the touch screen with the touch example.
meta: Open Board. From $18. A few stores.
